page: Vultr voc-g-96c-256gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores, supporting simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 256.0 GB, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU testing placing the instance in the top tier (top 10%) at 213,580.47. PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests also achieved top-tier placement. However, single-core performance is moderate; the stress-ng single-core test scored in the average tier, and single-threaded gzip compression registered in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient, reaching the top 10% at 8,120.31 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read and write speeds remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high compute density with a shared CPU allocation model, making it a cost-efficient option for highly parallelized workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations both demonstrated strong performance. The server is well-suited for multi-threaded processing, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference, though it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks.
